From: Sara Patel <sara@catalysthealth.com>

Subject: Request: isolation patterns & CAIQ artifacts for Dedicated/Private

Hi Diego,

Hope you’re doing well — Catalyst Health’s security team is working through the SIG/CAIQ for our procurement checklist and we need a short packet describing how Redwood handles network isolation and tenant separation for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically we’re looking for:

- A high-level network diagram that shows control plane vs data plane, inter-region routing, and any edge components.
- A concise description of the isolation model (tenant fencing, egress controls, KMS boundaries).
- A mapping of those controls to SIG/CAIQ question IDs (where possible) and any SOC 2 evidence pointers.

Do you have an index or a single PDF we can start with so our auditors know what to expect? If there’s a lightweight checklist we can hand to our third-party assessor, that would help us close the timeline.

Thanks — can we get an initial packet this week?

Best,
Sara Patel
Head of InfoSec, Catalyst Health
sara@catalysthealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

- Evidence pointers for SOC 2 controls (logging, KMS, audit trails).

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll share the index + high-level diagrams now (attached).
2) If you need deep-dive diagrams, we’ll queue a follow-up within 48 hours and share a secure Drive folder.

I’ve looped in Karthik (serving/runtime) and Mina (compliance) to own the technical mapping.

— Diego

Diego — quick notes for the packet we should send:

- Diagrams: include two views
  * "Control-vs-Data-plane-overview.pdf" (high-level)
  * "Edge-guard-topology_v3.drawio" (logical, shows egress proxies, NAT gateway separation, and optional air-gapped control plane)

- For private/VPC pictures, we should show logical VLANs and peering but not route table dumps.

I’ll prepare the draw.io topology and the segmentation matrix; Mina can add the CAIQ rows to the matrix. Attachments: edge-guard-topology_v3.drawio, segmentation_matrix_v2.xlsx.

Karthik

Hi Sara — attaching the initial packet as discussed. Files in this email: isolation_playbook_index.pdf, edge-guard-topology_v3.drawio (logical network diagram), segmentation_matrix_v2.xlsx.

Highlights from the packet:
- Control vs Data plane: The control plane (orchestrator, scheduler, and management APIs) is deployed in a logically separate subnet and only accessible via authenticated control channel (mTLS + customer-scoped IAM). Data plane GPUs and inference workers are in a separate tenancy pool; tenant fencing is enforced with network policies and workload identity.
- Egress policy: By default, Dedicated deployments use an egress gateway with egress whitelists; Private (VPC) deployments support customer-managed egress and optional NAT translation handled by customer.
- KMS boundaries: Customer keys are stored in a customer-managed KMS when requested (Private), otherwise per-tenant keys are stored with strict access controls and audit logs.
- Audit evidence: We included pointers to the SOC 2 binder in Drive and a short checklist auditors can use to validate network separation.

Quoted from Karthik’s note:

> We should show logical VLANs and peering but not route table dumps.

If your assessor prefers a single consolidated PDF for upload, we can generate that (redacting internal IDs) and provide a temporary read-only Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_shared_playbooks.

Would you like a 30-minute walkthrough with Karthik and Mina tomorrow to walk the auditor through the SIG mapping?

Best,
Diego
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
